facts.statement: Chubutinectes is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur known from the Late Cretaceous La Colonia Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: Chubutinectes (meaning "Chubut swimmer") is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous La Colonia Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Chubutinectes was discovered in 2009 on the Somún Curá plateau in Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The Chubutinectes holotype specimen, MPEF-PV 5232, was discovered in 2009 within sediments of the La Colonia Formation on the Somún Curá plateau in Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Chubutinectes carmeloi was described as a new genus and species in 2023 by O'Gorman and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2023, O'Gorman and colleagues described Chubutinectes carmeloi as a new genus and species of elasmosaurid plesiosaur based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The genus name Chubutinectes combines the name of the province Chubut with the Greek word for swimmer.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Chubutinectes", combines a reference to the Argentinean province "Chubut", where the holotype was found, with the Greek word "nectes", meaning "swimmer".

facts.statement: The species name carmeloi honors Carmelo Muñoz, who discovered the holotype.
facts.quote: The specific name, "carmeloi", honors Carmelo Muñoz, the discoverer of the holotype.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of disarticulated vertebrae, ribs, girdles, limb elements, and approximately 350 gastroliths.
facts.quote: The disarticulated specimen consists of cervical, pectoral, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebral centra and neural arches, various ribs, partial pectoral and pelvic girdles, fore- and hind-limb elements, and about 350 gastroliths.

facts.statement: The holotype is an immature specimen with a 1.4-meter-long dorsal region, suggesting it would have been larger than an adult Kawanectes.
facts.quote: The holotype of Chubutinectes is an osteologically immature specimen with a dorsal region measuring 1.4 m long, indicating that it was larger than an adult Kawanectes from the same formation.

facts.statement: Chubutinectes lived during the upper Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Chubutinectes was discovered in layers of the La Colonia Formation, which dates to the upper Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Chubutinectes lived less than 67.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Based on the presence of nanofossils of Micula spp., the rock layers are younger than around 67.3 million years old.

facts.statement: Unlike the estuarine-dwelling Kawanectes, Chubutinectes lived in marine environments.
facts.quote: En contraste a Kawanectes, el cual vivía en ambientes estuarinos, Chubutinectes vivía en ambientes marinos, lo que parece estar correlacionado con las diferencias en tamaño entre ambas especies.

facts.statement: Chubutinectes inhabited warm, relatively shallow neritic marine waters.
facts.quote: En particular, Chubutinectes habitaba ambientes neríticos de aguas cálidas y relativamente poco profundas.

facts.statement: The presence of gastroliths in the fossil record indicates Chubutinectes likely swallowed stones to aid digestion.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, C. carmeloi, known from a partial skeleton and associated gastroliths.

facts.statement: The cranial elements and anterior neck vertebrae of the holotype were likely lost to erosion.
facts.quote: Los elementos craneales y de la zona anterior del cuello habrían sido perdidos por erosión.

facts.statement: Chubutinectes is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
The time range for Chubutinectes is estimated between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
